decision_table_state_ownership.note: The unit of decision is the state class, not the product. Owner is the single authority for schema, migration and write authority.

rows.definition: New business state Actionist writes for the client product
rows.tenancy: tenant_id column plus RLS enforced in-engine
rows.rationale: A08 inferred, ecosystem fit, donor-stack compatibility, platform-owned policy removes the LLM-authored-RLS class
rows.falsifier: Loop 2 shows typed-port overhead exceeds direct access value for the pilot workload

rows.definition: State inside a mature donor kept as a running service
rows.tenancy: donor-native, host maps canonical to donor IDs explicitly
rows.rationale: The cost is the fork, not the database (SISOCRM observed). Upstream patches are the reason to stay downstream.
rows.falsifier: A donor whose operational burden exceeds its fork-avoidance saving

rows.definition: Donor code copied and owned; storage repointed at host Postgres
rows.rationale: SISOCRM 2026-07-31 absorption decision; enables real foreign keys between donor and owned records
rows.falsifier: Data-layer rewrite cost per donor measured in Loop 3 exceeds federation cost

rows.definition: Rich documents, blocks, whiteboards, realtime co-editing
rows.rationale: Deeply engineered; liability to own. Absorption adds the FK the donor lacks (page belongs to a deal permanently, not by folder convention).
rows.falsifier: Collaboration engine cannot expose a stable linkage key

rows.rationale: A12; the documented answer to losing cross-schema joins. Cross-owner mutation is never the mechanism.
rows.falsifier: A workflow where eventual consistency measurably breaks the client outcome

rows.rationale: Search and vector have converged commercially; one retrieval plane chosen for licence safety. Dedicated engines are licence-mined (Meilisearch MIT AND BUSL, Typesense GPL-3.0, Elasticsearch document-level security inside ELv2-only x-pack).
rows.falsifier: Pilot retrieval quality or latency demands a dedicated engine

rows.tenancy: naming and credential discipline only; no query semantics
rows.rationale: Object storage OSS is effectively closed (MinIO AGPL and archived, Garage AGPL); SeaweedFS is Apache-2.0 by elimination, a named concentration risk. SISOCRM left this undecided even at single-VPS scale.
rows.falsifier: n/a - this row is an open decision, not a settled default

rows.definition: Domain events, change feeds, integration triggers
rows.tenancy: subject or topic hierarchy mirroring the tenant boundary
rows.rationale: Outbox removes the enqueue-vs-commit race. NATS Apache-2.0 preferred over Redpanda BSL, whose Additional Use Grant excludes a Streaming or Queuing Service.
rows.falsifier: Event volume or ordering needs exceed a Postgres-outbox substrate

rows.definition: Sessions, locks, derived caches, local tool state
rows.tenancy: never a source of truth, so isolation is by lifetime
rows.rationale: SQLite is correct for bounded state owned end to end (SISOCRM observed)
rows.falsifier: Cache state becomes authoritative anywhere, which is a defect not a variant

invariants.statement: One authoritative owner per stateful resource, per table, per migration lineage, per file namespace, per event stream

invariants.falsifier: 80 percent of pilot state classes land on Postgres anyway and the port costs more than it saves

invariants.statement: Postgres is the default for new owned transactional state only, never imposed on donors
Cross-owner product views are event-fed read models, never cross-owner table mutation
Capabilities consume typed data ports; ORM choice is adapter-local
Migration authority is release-scoped; no release without a migration rollback path
Tenant identity is a first-class key on every owned resource from the first migration, with per-tenant key derivation for credential-class data

open_decisions.question: One database, schemas, service stores or hybrid per client
open_decisions.depends_on: reuse shape mix in the chosen pilot
open_decisions.note: SISOCRM answered schemas-per-donor for federation and one-schema for absorption; both were correct in context

open_decisions.question: What operations must the v1 typed data port support
open_decisions.candidate: port family (crud, query, tx, files, search, events) with capability-declared needs rather than one wide port

open_decisions.question: What mechanically prevents a capability writing a table it does not own
candidates: per-capability database roles with grants matching declared tables
RLS as the single authorization source binding host service and any API layer alike
static analysis of adapter declarations at admission
open_decisions.note: raised by this lane, proposed as a measured Loop-2 dimension

open_decisions.question: Host runtime language
open_decisions.note: ARCHITECTURE.md argues TypeScript control plane from a stratified 45-repo sample; not re-litigated here

rejected_here.claim: Force every donor onto Postgres and one ORM
rejected_here.reason: A09 and A10 already rejected; externally confirmed that the cost is the fork

rejected_here.claim: Adopt a multi-tenancy framework off the shelf for a TypeScript host
rejected_here.reason: None exist with real adoption; the only maintained ones are language-locked (Laravel, Django). Tenant isolation is bespoke work Actionist must own and test.

rejected_here.claim: Trust a licence badge or the GitHub API SPDX field
rejected_here.reason: Twelve-plus corrections this run; five surfaces where the API would mislead an automated pipeline
